ai.description: This frog reaches 55–60 mm. It is brown with a wrinkled, glandular dorsum and pale ventral spots. Distinctive features include a pointed snout and prominent, longitudinal skin ridges on the back.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus karnatakaensis* is best distinguished by its distinct, prominent, and highly rugose (wrinkled) skin texture, which is more pronounced than in other congeners.
ai.habitat: The Giant Wrinkled Frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Giant Wrinkled Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky streams and forest floors of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus karnatakaensis* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs on wet rocks near streams, which undergo direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus karnatakaensis* is endemic to the central Western Ghats in Karnataka, India, typically inhabiting streams at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Nyctibatrachus karnatakaensis* consists of a series of short, high-pitched "chirps" emitted by males from within fast-flowing forest streams.
